title: Present Continuous vs Present Simple: Dynamic & Stative
shortDescription: Contrast actions in progress and temporary situations with permanent habits and stative verbs.

title: Past Simple vs Past Continuous: Action & Background
shortDescription: Differentiate sequential completed past events from interrupted ongoing background scenes.

title: Present Perfect Simple: Recent Results & Life Experiences
shortDescription: Connect past actions to present consequences and discuss life experiences up to now.

title: Present Perfect Continuous: Duration & Ongoing Activity
shortDescription: Highlight ongoing duration, unfinished processes, and visible present side-effects.

title: Present Perfect Simple vs Continuous: Result vs Activity
shortDescription: Distinguish between completed quantity/outcome and uninterrupted ongoing duration.

title: Duration Questions & Time Frames: How Long, For and Since
shortDescription: Ask about continuing situations and specify duration starting points versus total periods.

title: Present Perfect vs Past Simple: Open vs Finished Time
shortDescription: Select correctly between past finished time markers and open, current time relevance.

title: Past Perfect Simple: The Earlier Past in Narrative
shortDescription: Establish chronological clarity when an action occurred before another past milestone.

title: Past Perfect Continuous: Cause & Duration Before a Past Point
shortDescription: Explain earlier continuous activities that produced visible past outcomes.

title: Possession & States: Have and Have Got
shortDescription: Use have and have got for possession, relationships, illnesses, and habitual actions.

title: Past Habits & States: Used to
shortDescription: Contrast discontinued past habits and states with present realities.

title: Arrangements & Intentions: Present Tenses and Going to
shortDescription: Distinguish fixed personal arrangements from planned prior intentions and physical evidence.

title: Instant Decisions & Offers: Will and Shall
shortDescription: Employ will for spontaneous decisions, offers, promises, and shall for first-person suggestions.

title: Predictions & Plans: Will vs Going to
shortDescription: Contrast belief-based predictions with predictions grounded in visible present clues.

title: Future in Progress & Completion: Will Be Doing and Will Have Done
shortDescription: Describe actions ongoing at a specific future moment and actions completed prior to a deadline.

title: Future Time & Conditional Clauses: When, As Soon As, If
shortDescription: Apply present forms in subordinate clauses of time and condition referring to the future.

title: Ability & Possibility: Can, Could and Be Able To
shortDescription: Express general ability versus specific past successful achievements with managed to / was able to.

title: Past Opportunity & Unrealised Action: Could Have Done
shortDescription: Discuss actions that were possible in the past but were not actually carried out.

title: Logical Deduction: Must and Can't
shortDescription: Formulate strong logical certainty and impossibility based on present evidence.

title: Possibility & Speculation: May and Might
shortDescription: Indicate tentative possibility in present and future contexts, and retrospective speculation.

title: Obligation & Necessity: Must and Have to
shortDescription: Differentiate internal personal obligation from external authority, rules, or laws.

title: Prohibition & Absence of Obligation: Mustn't vs Needn't
shortDescription: Contrast strict prohibition with lack of necessity (needn't / don't have to / didn't need to).

title: Advice, Expectation & Warning: Should, Ought to, Had Better
shortDescription: Give sensible advice, express past regret (should have done), and issue urgent warnings.

title: Hypothetical Actions & Past Habits: Would
shortDescription: Employ would for imaginary situations, past recurring actions, and polite willingness.

title: Social Formulae: Requests, Offers, Permission & Invitations
shortDescription: Select appropriate degrees of politeness in everyday spoken communicative scenarios.

title: Real vs Hypothetical: If I do vs If I did
shortDescription: Contrast open real possibilities with improbable hypothetical present or future scenarios.

title: Unreal Present & Regret: If I knew and I wish I knew
shortDescription: Formulate counterfactual present states and express discontent about current circumstances.

title: Past Regret & Third Conditional: If I had known
shortDescription: Analyse unfulfilled past conditions and their impossible consequences in retrospective evaluation.

title: Desire for Change & Annoyance: Wish + Would
shortDescription: Express frustration about current annoying habits and desire for another agent to change behavior.

title: Passive Formation: Present & Past Simple
shortDescription: Shift discourse focus to the patient/recipient of action across basic tenses.

title: Complex Passives: Continuous, Perfect and Modal Structures
shortDescription: Construct passive sentences with being done, have been done, and modal auxiliaries.

title: Impersonal Reporting: It is said that / He is said to
shortDescription: Use formal distance in news and reporting with introductory passive matrices and nominative infinitives.

title: Causative Services: Have Something Done
shortDescription: Express arranging for professional services or suffering misfortune with have/get + object + V3.

title: Reported Statements: Tense Backshift & Time References
shortDescription: Accurately adjust verb tenses, pronouns, and time/place adverbs in indirect statements.

title: Reported Questions, Orders & Reporting Verb Patterns
shortDescription: Form indirect questions with whether/if and deploy advanced verbs (admit, deny, advise, warn).

title: Direct Question Formation & Preposition Stranding
shortDescription: Structure complex questions and leave dependent prepositions naturally at sentence ends.

title: Indirect Questions: Do you know where...? / He asked me where...
shortDescription: Maintain affirmative word order inside polite embedded and indirect question clauses.

title: Auxiliary Substitution: So do I, Neither do I, I think so
shortDescription: Avoid clunky repetition using auxiliary echo responses, inverted agreement, and pro-form so/not.

title: Question Tags: Seeking Confirmation vs Real Questions
shortDescription: Match polarity correctly and modulate intonation between genuine inquiries and casual checks.

title: Verb + -ing: Enjoy, Mind, Suggest
shortDescription: Identify verbs systematically taking gerund complements and practice idiomatic usage.

title: Verb + to-Infinitive: Decide, Forget, Promise
shortDescription: Master verbs followed by to-infinitive including prospective decisions and commitments.

title: Verb + Object + to-Infinitive: Want someone to do, Advise
shortDescription: Structure manipulative and advisory verbs followed by noun object and infinitive clause.

title: Meaning Shifts: Remember, Regret, Stop doing vs to do
shortDescription: Discriminate crucial semantic differences when complement changes from -ing to to-infinitive.

title: Subtle Pattern Differences: Try, Need, Help
shortDescription: Grasp nuanced complementations: experiment vs attempt (try) and passive meaning (need doing).

title: Preferences: Like doing vs Like to do, Would like
shortDescription: Distinguish enjoyment of activity from prudent habitual choices and conditional desires.

title: Expressing Preference: Prefer and Would Rather
shortDescription: Compare options using prefer ... to ... and would rather ... than with base verb forms.

title: Preposition + -ing: Before leaving, Instead of waiting
shortDescription: Apply the inviolable rule that prepositions must be followed by a gerund when taking verbal objects.

title: Familiarity: Be Used to and Get Used to doing
shortDescription: Separate psychological familiarity (be used to + -ing) from discontinued past habits (used to + inf).

title: Verb + Preposition + -ing: Succeed in, Insist on
shortDescription: Combine dependent verbal prepositions smoothly with downstream gerund phrases.

title: Special -ing Idioms: There's no point in, Worth, Have difficulty
shortDescription: Learn high-frequency colloquial formulas governing fixed gerund expressions.

title: Expressing Purpose: To do, For doing, and So that
shortDescription: Articulate intention and function cleanly using infinitives of purpose or finite so that clauses.

title: Adjective + to-Infinitive: Difficult to do, Glad to hear
shortDescription: Link evaluation and emotional reaction adjectives to following explanatory infinitive phrases.

title: Specific Nuance: Afraid to do vs Afraid of doing
shortDescription: Contrast deliberate unwillingness to act with apprehension of involuntary accidents.

title: Perception Verbs: See somebody do vs See somebody doing
shortDescription: Distinguish between witnessing a complete event and perceiving an action in mid-progress.

title: -ing Participle Clauses: Feeling tired, he went to bed
shortDescription: Condense complex background causes and simultaneous actions using adverbial participle clauses.

title: Countable vs Uncountable Nouns & Category Shifts
shortDescription: Navigate dual-membership nouns whose countability alters their meaning (coffee, experience, paper).

title: Singular & Plural Reference: A/An with Countable, Some with Uncountable
shortDescription: Deploy indefinite determiners properly according to noun number and countability status.

title: Specific vs Non-Specific Reference: A/An vs The
shortDescription: Master hearer-shared knowledge and contextual uniqueness determining the definite article.

title: Institutional Zero Article: School vs The School, Bed vs The Bed
shortDescription: Contrast primary institutional purpose (go to prison) with reference to physical buildings.

title: General Classes vs Particular Groups: Children vs The Children, The Giraffe
shortDescription: Use zero article for universal plural generic claims and definite article for representative species.

title: Proper Names & Geography with and without The
shortDescription: Command conventions governing oceans, mountain ranges, individual peaks, streets, and hotels.

title: Noun Forms: Plurals, Noun + Noun Compounds, and Possessive 's vs Of
shortDescription: Determine when to use apostrophe possessive versus prepositional of phrases and noun premodifiers.

title: Reflexives & Independence: Myself, On my own, By myself
shortDescription: Employ reflexive pronouns for co-referential actions and emphatic independence.

title: Existential and Anticipatory: There vs It
shortDescription: Distinguish new entity introduction with there from referential and dummy it expressions.

title: Assertive vs Non-Assertive: Some, Any, and Indefinite Compounds
shortDescription: Select some in positive invitations and any in negative, interrogative, or arbitrary contexts.

title: Quantifiers: Much/Many vs Few/A few, Little/A little
shortDescription: Differentiate positive perspective (a few/a little) from restrictive negative scarcity (few/little).

title: Binary Distributives: Both, Neither, and Either (of)
shortDescription: Accurately coordinate two entities and ensure correct subject-verb agreement.

title: Universal Quantifiers: All, Most, Whole, Every, and Each
shortDescription: Distinguish collective totality from individual distributivity across varying noun patterns.

title: Relative Pronouns: Who, That, and Which
shortDescription: Introduce restrictive relative clauses identifying specific persons versus objects.

title: Contact Clauses: Omission of Object Relative Pronouns
shortDescription: Identify when relative pronouns function as grammatical objects and can be omitted naturally.

title: Relative Adverbs & Possessives: Whose, Whom, and Where
shortDescription: Link possession, formal prepositional objects, and spatial antecedents inside relative clauses.

title: Essential vs Extra Information: Defining and Non-Defining Relative Clauses
shortDescription: Master punctuation, comma intonation, and pronoun restrictions (never that in extra-info).

title: Reduced Relatives: -ing and -ed Participial Postmodifiers
shortDescription: Streamline complex clauses into concise active (-ing) and passive (-ed) postmodifiers.

title: Participle Adjectives (-ing/-ed) and Adjective Ordering
shortDescription: Contrast causing feelings with experiencing them, and sequence multiple descriptive adjectives.

title: Adjectives vs Adverbs & Irregulars: Quick/Quickly, Well, Fast, Hard/Hardly
shortDescription: Identify linking verb complements and avoid confusion between lookalikes like hard and hardly.

title: Degree Modifiers: So, Such, Enough, and Too
shortDescription: Construct consequential result clauses with so/such ... that and calibrate sufficiency/excess.

title: Grading Adverbs: Quite, Pretty, Rather, and Fairly
shortDescription: Calibrate subjective evaluation and unexpectedness across moderate grading adverbs.

title: Comparative Forms & Modifiers: Much better, Far more, Any better
shortDescription: Qualify differences using degree submodifiers like slightly, considerably, and nowhere near.

title: Comparisons of Equality & Superlatives: As...as, Than, The most
shortDescription: Express equivalence, proportional changes (the more... the better), and superlative boundaries.

title: Clause Order: Verb + Object, Sequencing Place and Time
shortDescription: Prevent constituent splitting between transitive verb and object, and sequence place before time.

title: Adverb Positions: Mid-Position with Auxiliaries and Main Verbs
shortDescription: Place frequency and certainty adverbs accurately before lexical verbs and after auxiliaries/be.

title: Temporal Adverbs: Still, Yet, Already, and Any More
shortDescription: Contribute aspectual expectations to discourse regarding persistence, completion, and cessation.

title: Focus & Surprise: Even and Even Though / Even If
shortDescription: Highlight extreme cases and unexpected contrasts using the focusing particle even.

title: Concession & Contrast: Although, Though, Even though, Despite, In spite of
shortDescription: Differentiate clausal connectives from prepositional phrases taking noun phrases or gerunds.

title: Precaution & Anticipation: In case
shortDescription: Distinguish precautionary actions taken in advance from conditional responses (in case vs if).

title: Conditional Connectives: Unless, As long as, Provided that
shortDescription: Formulate negative conditions (if not) and explicit stipulations across formal and informal discourse.

title: Manner & Comparison: As, Like, and As if / As though
shortDescription: Contrast prepositional comparison (like + noun) with conjunctional clauses and unreal manner.

title: Time Relations: During, While, For, and By vs Until
shortDescription: Disentangle prepositional spans (during/for), clausal overlap (while), and deadlines vs duration.

title: Time Prepositions: At, On, In, In time vs On time, At the end
shortDescription: Master clock times, calendar dates, periods, punctuality vs margins, and endpoint expressions.

title: Position & Space: In, At, and On in Context
shortDescription: Conceptualise 3D containment, 2D surfaces, and functional interaction points accurately.

title: Direction & Movement: To, At, In, and Into
shortDescription: Coordinate verbs of trajectory, arrival, and penetration across varied spatial contexts.

title: Idiomatic Spatial Uses & Means: Other uses of In/On/At and By
shortDescription: Apply fixed idiomatic idioms (by car, by chance, on purpose, in a hurry, at risk).

title: Dependent Nouns: Reason for, Cause of, Demand for
shortDescription: Master noun-complement preposition pairings essential for academic and formal clarity.

title: Dependent Adjectives: Proud of, Interested in, Afraid of, Good at
shortDescription: Internalise natural collocational bonds between evaluation adjectives and their governing prepositions.

title: Dependent Verbs: Listen to, Look at, Depend on, Suffer from
shortDescription: Consolidate idiomatic prepositional verb bonds across everyday conversational verbs.

title: Phrasal Verbs Anatomy: Separability & Pronoun Placement
shortDescription: Grasp particle movement rules: object placement and obligatory split with object pronouns.

title: Particles In and Out: Movement, Completion & Discovery
shortDescription: Explore core and metaphorical dimensions of in and out (check in, drop in, find out, run out).

title: Particles On and Off: Activation, Continuation & Departure
shortDescription: Command phrasal meanings related to progress, cancellation, and departures (carry on, call off).

title: Particles Up and Down: Increase, Decrease, Destruction & Completion
shortDescription: Master vertical metaphors and telic completion with up/down (turn up, break down, give up).

title: Particles Away and Back: Distance, Return & Removal
shortDescription: Deploy motion and reciprocal particles in dialogue (run away, give away, get back, pay back).

title: B1–B2 Master Diagnostic Review
shortDescription: Comprehensive evaluation testing contrasting tenses, complex modals, passives, conditionals, and verb patterns.
